observable_outcome: internal/provider carries, for all three adapter names, one shared contract-fixture table covering validation.md's nine adapter cases; a three-slot Provider account pool that holds no credential value and no threshold number and reads no clock; a per-Provider usage window that is separate from internal/quota and from the runner's cost ledger and carries no monetary vocabulary; a circuit breaker whose opening classes are the table in dp-v2-027 d12, whose closing never depends on elapsed time alone, and whose state names this Loop's own decision rather than the Provider's condition; and a provider-neutral handoff that converts back into a Request for the target adapter and fails closed when the Increment, Artifact or Verification content it carried does not survive the conversion. No Provider CLI is invoked beyond reading --version and --help, no real Provider response is written to any file, and the evidence states in a table which of M6's four completion conditions this task does not satisfy and that V2-028 owns them.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope table, written before any code is changed. The evidence opens with a table with one row per M6 completion condition, taken verbatim from docs/architecture/roadmap.md's M6 section, stating for each what this task makes true, what it does not, and who owns the remainder, using the attribution in dp-v2-027 d16. Condition 1 and condition 4 must be stated as wholly V2-028's with gate rules G3.1 and G3.3 cited as the reason. The phrase capability exercised must not appear anywhere in the evidence, in any code comment, or in the runbook; assert its absence with a grep over the files this task wrote and record the argv. Nothing in the evidence may claim or imply that this task passes any release gate.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything, by the implementer and not copied from this Work Order. Record the top-level test names and counts of internal/provider, internal/runner, internal/reconciler and internal/quota as measured with go test -count=1 -v on the starting commit, and record the starting commit. Every pre-existing test must still pass at the end under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged, and the before and after top-level counts per touched package must both be reported. If any measured baseline count disagrees with what this Work Order implies anywhere, the measurement wins and the disagreement is recorded.

A3. Adapter argv surface, measured with help output only. Run codex --version, opencode --version, codex exec --help and opencode run --help, and record the verbatim flag list each help output declares. Do not run codex exec or opencode run themselves for any reason. Then set each adapter's flags to exactly the subset that help declares and that is required for non-interactive execution and structured JSON on stdout. Remove any flag help does not declare. If a property the adapter needs has no flag in help, do not invent one and do not substitute a similar one: record the gap and escalate. The claude adapter's argv is not changed at all; record that its four existing arguments are unchanged and cite the live records that measured them.

A4. Workspace pinning is not re-expressed as a flag. Assert for all three adapters that Invocation.WorkingDirectory equals the request workspace, that no argv element is an absolute path other than argv[0], that no argv element contains a path traversal segment, a NUL, a carriage return or a newline, and that Build refuses a workspace containing any of those. Record that ProcessSupervisor and NamespaceConfinement are what hold the boundary and that the adapter's job is only to be unable to ask to leave it.

A5. The nine-case fixture matrix, as one table over three adapter values. Create internal/provider/testdata fixtures for: success; explicit model error; quota or usage exhaustion; non-zero exit; zero exit with an error envelope; empty structured output; malformed structured output; usage reported; usage not reported; and CLI version incompatibility. Timeout and cancel are covered through ClassifyError and NormalizeError rather than a file. Drive every case through every adapter from a single table, and assert per cell the expected Succeeded, FailureClass, Retryable and Ambiguous. Report how many distinct table drivers exist in the package and assert it is one for this matrix: three near-identical copies satisfy the assertions while defeating the purpose, which is that a change to build or parseFixture visibly reaches all three.

A6. Usage reported and usage not reported are distinguishable. Assert that a fixture whose usage object is absent produces a Result a caller can tell apart from a fixture whose usage object is present with zero counts, and that the usage window in A9 treats the absent case as unknown rather than as zero consumption. State in the evidence which representation was chosen and why it does not change any existing assertion about Result.Usage.

A7. Fixtures are secret-free by construction and by measurement. Every file under internal/provider/testdata must: be smaller than provider.MaxFixtureBytes; contain no value for output, result or summary other than the empty string or the literal sha256 followed by a colon and 64 lowercase hex digits; match neither the package's forbidden pattern nor its secret pattern; and contain no JSON key matching the credential deny list from A8. Assert all four mechanically over every file the directory contains, discovered by walking the directory rather than by a hardcoded list, and fail outright on a zero-file walk. State in the evidence that no fixture was derived from any real Provider response and that shape_source in the manifest declares that for every entry.

A8. A source guard for internal/provider, modelled on internal/runner/source_guard_test.go. Parse every non-test .go file in the package with go/parser, fail outright on a zero-file scan, and assert: no import of os/exec, net, net/http, net/url, internal/domain, internal/runner, internal/application or internal/quota; no struct field name and no json tag matching the credential deny list; and no identifier in the package named healthy, unhealthy, broken, down, up, alive, dead or ok. Verify the deny-list matcher against a known-positive and a known-negative name first, as the runner's own test does, so a matcher that matches nothing cannot pass.

A9. The Provider account pool. Exactly three slots, keyed by the adapter names codex, claude and opencode, with no fourth slot constructible and no fourth adapter type added to the package. A slot holds only the fields dp-v2-027 d8 lists. Assert: no field holds a credential value, an environment value, a token, a session identifier, an owner identity, an executable path or a threshold number; Acquire and Release take an explicit time argument and the package reads no clock in any non-test file; a second Acquire of an in-use slot is refused rather than queued; Release of a slot that is not held is refused; and the per-Provider concurrency ceiling is one by construction, asserted by there being no code path that returns two live handles for one name. Record that the preflight record is referenced by id only and that no limit value is copied out of it.

A10. The usage window. Per Provider, per named window, counting invocations attempted through the pool and the token counts the Provider reported, with not-reported distinct from zero, against a ceiling the caller supplies, reporting only within-window, exhausted or unknown. Assert: no exported or unexported identifier and no emitted JSON key in the package contains any of usd, cost, price, billing, spend, budget or credit, checked as a case-insensitive substring scan over the package's declared names and over the marshalled keys of every type the package emits; a window rollover is driven by the time argument the caller passes and never by a stored clock; and exhausted is reached exactly one unit over the ceiling and not before. State explicitly in the evidence, in one paragraph, that this window is not internal/quota (the Firestore daily free-tier reservation, which this task does not edit) and not internal/runner.CostLedger (the runner-local, owner-approved, fail-closed runaway detector whose observation boundary docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md records), and that it never decides whether a process may start and never claims to know a subscription's remaining allowance.

A11. The circuit breaker's opening table. Implement exactly the mapping in dp-v2-027 d12 and assert it as a table with one row per class, covering every value of internal/provider.FailureClass and, as a documented mapping only, every one of domain.FailureClass's seventeen values. Assert that the table is exhaustive over the provider-local class set by construction: a new class added to the package without a row must make the test fail. Do not import internal/domain to do this; the domain side of the mapping is a declared table in the test and in the runbook. Assert per row: opens immediately, counts toward a windowed threshold, opens only the narrower Provider-and-model circuit, moves the pool slot without opening, or neither counts nor opens.

A12. Closing is never time alone. Assert: open to half-open requires the cooldown deadline passed under the caller's time argument and a probe token the pool issues, and that exactly one probe token can be outstanding at a time; that for an open caused by a quota class the window must also have rolled over, proven by a case where the deadline has passed but the window has not rolled and no probe is issued; that half-open reaches closed only after a reported successful observation and never on issuing the probe; that a failed probe multiplies the cooldown up to a declared ceiling and does not reset the counter; that a contract-incompatible open is never probe-eligible and closes only on an explicitly observed change of declared CLI version; and that a quarantined or stopped-for-inspection slot has no probe and no deadline that can move it. Every one of these must be driven by an injected time argument. No fixed sleep, no timer, no goroutine.

A13. An open breaker does not read as a broken Provider. Assert the exported state set is exactly sending, not-sending and probing; that every not-sending value carries the closed set of classes that produced it, the window the count was taken over, and an observation_scope value; and that the observation_scope value states in words that only invocations that passed through this Loop's own execution path were counted. Record in the evidence the measured precedent this follows: docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md's observation-boundary section, including its recorded example of six real claude invocations run by hand that the ledger never saw.

A14. The handoff conversion. Keep PrepareHandoff and its existing assertion unchanged in meaning. Add Handoff.Validate, the content digest over IncrementID, Constraints, Decisions, Artifacts, Verification and Unresolved, and RequestFromHandoff. Assert, for all six ordered pairs of the three Provider names: the target Request's packet compares equal to the source packet field by field, including every Artifact name and digest and every Verification entry; that mutating any one of those carried fields between PrepareHandoff and RequestFromHandoff is refused rather than silently accepted; that RequestFromHandoff refuses a target name outside the three; that it refuses when the target's breaker is not sending; that a chain of two handoffs preserves the first failure class in the bounded history; that handing back to a Provider already present in the history for the same Increment is refused; and that the target's Result carries the target's own Provider name and its own output digest rather than the one the handoff carried. Assert the Handoff and history types have no field able to hold a prompt, a response, a session identifier or free text, and that the history is bounded with a stated bound.

A15. The fixture provenance manifest. internal/provider/testdata/manifest.json carries one entry per fixture with provider, cli_version_declared, shape_source, observed_at, reason and corresponding_live_exercise. Assert every fixture file in the directory has exactly one manifest entry and every entry has exactly one file, by walking the directory. Assert shape_source is projected-shape-hand-authored for every entry in this task and that corresponding_live_exercise names provider-live-multi. Record the measured --version output for each of the three CLIs next to the declared version.

A16. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test or non-test file in the package; every timestamp and every deadline comparison comes from a value the caller passes in. Assert mechanically that no non-test file in internal/provider references time.Now, time.Sleep, time.After, time.Tick, time.NewTimer, time.NewTicker or the go statement. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/provider three times in sequence and record that the verdict line and the output are identical each time, and once with -race.

A17. Existing tests and downstream packages. internal/provider's three existing top-level tests keep their names and their assertions, and internal/runner and internal/reconciler still pass unchanged: internal/runner/costledger_test.go TestClaudeAdapterParseRejectsRealShapeButProjectionSucceeds and internal/runner/journey_test.go both depend on CodexAdapter and ClaudeAdapter behaviour and must not be edited. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/runner ./internal/reconciler and record the verdict. If any change to internal/provider would require editing a file under internal/runner to keep it green, stop and escalate rather than editing it: internal/runner is prohibited here for the G6b reason in dp-v2-027 d10 and d18.

A18. The live-exercise intersection is measured and reported, not repaired. Read .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-075-live-exercise-files.json, compute the intersection between its published paths and this task's own diff using the argv that file's reproduction block declares, and record the result. It will be non-empty because internal/provider/adapters.go, provider.go and handoff.go are members of the set. State that this makes ev-v2-075-provider-live-claude-rebind require re-observation under gate rule G6b, that V2-028 owns that re-observation, and that V2-075's ledger is exhausted so a new owner-approved record and a new ledger path are required. Do not touch .agents/v2/provider-preflight/**, do not run any live suite, and do not adjust any threshold.

A19. Component evidence keys, as a transitive closure. Measure devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final formatted tree with every touched file git-added, and record which component keys moved relative to the starting commit. The expected set is provider, runner, reconciler, api, control-plane and store-firestore from the internal/provider edit, plus docs and task-ledger from the runbook and ledger edits; if the measurement disagrees with that set, the measurement wins and the difference is recorded. Issue one evidence record, for the component provider, whose evidence_key is the provider key read from that final measurement. Record the other movements as a measured note under gate rule G6a naming the argv, and do not create a second evidence record for a component this task did not verify.

A20. The runbook. docs/operations/provider-adapters.md is written in Japanese prose with English identifiers and says nothing the code does not do. It must state: the measured argv surface of each of the three adapters and how it was measured; that the fixtures are hand-authored to the projected shape and never a real response, and what the manifest fields mean; the breaker's opening table over both taxonomies and the fact that closing is never time alone; that an open breaker is this Loop's decision and not a statement about the Provider, with the observation boundary named; the difference between the usage window, internal/quota and the runner's cost ledger; and which of M6's completion conditions this task does not satisfy, with V2-028 named. Do not edit docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md or docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md.

A21. Evidence is registered and the ledger test is green. Append exactly one entry to .agents/v2/evidence/index.json for .agents/v2/evidence/V2-027-provider.json, with result passed and evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of that file's final committed bytes, and touch no other task's entry. task_id is V2-027, the producer. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts and record that TestTaskPacketsValidate, TestActiveEvidenceIndex and TestProviderPreflightLedgerPassesOnTheRealTree all pass.

A22. A skipped test is never counted as a pass, per gate rule G7. Record every skip explicitly with status skipped and its reason. Record the execution environment identifiers: hostname, uname -sr, the go version as resolved inside devbox run --pure, and the measured --version output of each of the three Provider CLIs together with the absolute path each resolves to.

A23. Secret scan before commit. Run devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml on the working tree before committing, and separately scan the other subtrees this task wrote by naming them (internal/provider and docs). Do not run gitleaks dir . -- it walks the gitignored build/evidence output and makes the tracked state unreadable. If a finding appears, fix the file rather than widening .gitleaks.toml; that file is not edited by this task.

A24. make check is green after the evidence commit. Commit this task's files, then run devbox run --pure -- make check and record the verdict, so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. If make check is red because of a manifest or component check, stop and escalate rather than editing ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*.

A25. Nothing outside the fixture layer is claimed. Assert and record that no Provider CLI subcommand was executed at any point (only --version and --help), that no cost ledger file was created or written, that no entry was added to any file under .agents/v2/provider-preflight/, and that no Google Cloud resource was touched. If any acceptance item above cannot be satisfied as written, stop and escalate to the tech_lead with the measurement that shows why, rather than weakening it, rewording it, or recording it as passed.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Do not perform any operation that loses work that has not been committed. If history has to be rebuilt, show that nothing is lost and report it.

Do not start a real Provider CLI. Reading codex --version, opencode --version, codex exec --help and opencode run --help is permitted and required by A3 because it consumes no Provider usage and needs no authentication; running codex exec, opencode run or claude with a prompt is forbidden for any reason, including to check whether a flag works.

Do not attempt to authenticate codex or opencode. Authentication uses the owner's subscription identity and no agent may perform it; the unauthenticated state is a fact this task records, not a defect it fixes.
Do not write a real Provider response, a prompt, or any conversation text into any file, test, comment or evidence field. Any output metadata is a sha256 digest and nothing else.
Do not record a credential value in any form -- not in a field, not in a fixture, not in a log line, not in evidence, not in a comment.
Do not touch internal/domain. No FailureClass constant is added there; dp-v2-027 d17 records why the V2-049 precedent argues against it rather than for it.

Do not touch internal/quota. It is the Firestore daily free-tier reservation, it is the roots of the infra component whose reverse closure is eight components, and internal/quota/quota.go is a member of the published live exercise file set.
Do not touch internal/runner. The per-Provider projection from a real CLI response belongs to V2-028, which can measure one.
Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. If a manifest or component check turns red, stop and escalate; do not edit them.
Do not touch contracts/release-contract/** and do not weaken any capability declaration. Do not remove codex or opencode from any providers list to make a check pass.
Do not touch contracts/schemas/**, contracts/fixtures/** or contracts/openapi/**. The fixtures for this task live under internal/provider/testdata.

Do not edit .agents/v2/task-state/**, .agents/v2/packets/** or .agents/v2/provider-preflight/**. The coordinator records transitions and packets, and editing an approved preflight record breaks its approval digest binding by design.
Do not edit .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/**. The V2-075 exercise file set is read, never modified.

Do not copy any numeric threshold out of a provider-preflight record into code, a fixture, a read model or the runbook. Reaching a threshold is a stop for inspection, never a success, never a failure, and never a billing event.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine. Waiting is bounded deadline polling over an injected clock value, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip with its reason and record the execution environment identifiers.

Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating, reweighting or weakening it.

Every pre-existing test keeps passing under its existing name with its existing assertions unchanged. Measure the baseline counts yourself; do not copy a count from this Work Order, and if a measurement disagrees with anything implied here, the measurement wins and the disagreement is recorded.

The phrase capability exercised must not appear in this task's evidence, code comments or runbook. This task produces contract-fixture evidence, which gate rule G3.3 says satisfies no real-environment condition at any grade.

When a digest appears in prose, write it as 64 or 40 lowercase hex digits with at most one punctuation character after it, and never two adjacent dots; the secret-scan allowlist for .agents/v2 is narrowed to that shape.
Scan with devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml before committing, naming the subtree. Do not use gitleaks dir . and do not widen .gitleaks.toml.
Do not touch any Google Cloud resource. Nothing in this task needs one.
